      "nets": ["Net-(D37-K2)", "NET0170", "U44 Y output", "GND"],
      "observed": "D37 channel 2 has its anode (A2, pin 4) on NET0170 and its cathode (K2, pin 2) through R64 to NET0170. Both ends of that LED path sit on the same driven node, so channel 2 can never be forward-biased. Channel 1 is wired as intended: K1 goes through R57 to GND.",
      "expected": "The second LED channel's cathode resistor should return to GND, as R57 does for channel 1, so the LED can conduct when U44 drives its anode.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"121\") (name \"NET0170\") ... (node (ref \"D37\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") ... (node (ref \"R64\") (pin \"2\") ... (node (ref \"U44\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"176\") (name \"Net-(D37-K2)\") ... (node (ref \"D37\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"K2\") ... (node (ref \"R64\") (pin \"1\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R64 Net-_D37-K2_ NET0170 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The second LED of the dual indicator never lights, so the status indication for that channel is lost.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["U14", "Q7", "R7"],
      "pins": ["U14.2", "U14.1", "Q7.1"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "5V_CAN_ENABLE", "Net-(Q7-G)"],
      "observed": "The tri-state buffer U14 has its data input A (pin 2) tied to the +5V rail. Its output Y drives the gate of Q7, the P-channel switch that feeds 5V_switched_CAN. With A at +5V, Y can only be high or high-impedance, and R7 also pulls the gate to +5V, so Q7 is always off.",
      "expected": "The enable buffer's data input should be a logic-low level (e.g. GND) or a control signal, so that asserting 5V_CAN_ENABLE pulls the Q7 gate low and switches the CAN transceiver supply on.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+5V\") ... (node (ref \"U14\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"input\")) ... (node (ref \"U14\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"VCC\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"189\") (name \"Net-(Q7-G)\") ... (node (ref \"Q7\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"G\") ... (node (ref \"R7\") (pin \"2\") ... (node (ref \"U14\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"50\") (name \"5V_CAN_ENABLE\") ... (node (ref \"U14\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"/OE\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "The 5V_switched_CAN rail that powers the isolated CAN side cannot be enabled, so the CAN transceiver side stays unpowered.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["U19", "U41"],
      "pins": ["U19.4", "U19.5", "U41.4", "U41.5"],
      "nets": ["GND"],
      "observed": "Both isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated-side ground pins GND2 (pin 5) and logic-side ground pins GND1 (pin 4) on the same GND net. The bus-side reference is therefore not isolated from the logic ground.",
      "expected": "In an isolated CAN transceiver, GND2 (and VCC2) belong to a separate isolated ground domain (for example GND_ISO) and must not be tied to the logic GND.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U19\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"GND1\") (pintype \"power_in\")) (node (ref \"U19\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"GND2\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U41\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"GND1\") (pintype \"power_in\")) (node (ref \"U41\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"GND2\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver"}
      ],
      "impact": "The galvanic isolation that the CAN interfaces are meant to provide is defeated, so the bus ground is directly tied to the controller ground.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows several candidate deviations, the strongest being an LED channel whose cathode resistor returns to its own anode node (D37/R64). Other candidates are the CAN-supply enable buffer U14 with its data input tied to +5V, and the isolated CAN transceivers' GND2 tied to logic GND. Each is supported by specific netlist connections, but none is fully conclusive."
}

anomalies.observed: D37 channel 2 has its anode (A2, pin 4) on NET0170 and its cathode (K2, pin 2) through R64 to NET0170. Both ends of that LED path sit on the same driven node, so channel 2 can never be forward-biased. Channel 1 is wired as intended: K1 goes through R57 to GND.
anomalies.expected: The second LED channel's cathode resistor should return to GND, as R57 does for channel 1, so the LED can conduct when U44 drives its anode.
anomalies.impact: The second LED of the dual indicator never lights, so the status indication for that channel is lost.

anomalies.observed: The tri-state buffer U14 has its data input A (pin 2) tied to the +5V rail. Its output Y drives the gate of Q7, the P-channel switch that feeds 5V_switched_CAN. With A at +5V, Y can only be high or high-impedance, and R7 also pulls the gate to +5V, so Q7 is always off.
anomalies.expected: The enable buffer's data input should be a logic-low level (e.g. GND) or a control signal, so that asserting 5V_CAN_ENABLE pulls the Q7 gate low and switches the CAN transceiver supply on.
anomalies.impact: The 5V_switched_CAN rail that powers the isolated CAN side cannot be enabled, so the CAN transceiver side stays unpowered.

anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated-side ground pins GND2 (pin 5) and logic-side ground pins GND1 (pin 4) on the same GND net. The bus-side reference is therefore not isolated from the logic ground.
anomalies.expected: In an isolated CAN transceiver, GND2 (and VCC2) belong to a separate isolated ground domain (for example GND_ISO) and must not be tied to the logic GND.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation that the CAN interfaces are meant to provide is defeated, so the bus ground is directly tied to the controller ground.
